clue.text: King in haste arranged interview as option in 10 1 down

indicators.note: the king's letter goes in among the letters of haste
the letters of king-plus-haste are arranged into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
an audience is a formal interview with a dignitary

explanation.surface: A monarch in a hurry sets up a meeting as one of his options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns K plus HASTE into ASKTHE. 10 1 down is the quiz show answering 10 and 1 down; asking the studio audience is one of its lifelines.
explanation.definitionFit: Polling the studio crowd is one of the lifelines a contestant may use on the quiz show.

clue.text: See 10
Strong points for which there's no return

explanation.surface: Fortified positions, once taken, are never given back.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the idiom 'for keeps', meaning permanently, with nothing handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle strongholds are keeps, and something given for keeps is never returned.

clue.text: Think to follow greeting at the end of a month

indicators.note: the thinking word is placed to follow the greeting

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
ween is an archaic verb meaning think or suppose

explanation.surface: Someone ponders what to say after saying hello at the close of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: All Hallows' Eve falls on 31 October, the last day of that month.

clue.text: I leave note in plane to provide shrub

indicators.note: the note goes in the shortened plane
the letter I is told to leave the aircraft word

parts.note: an Airbus is a make of passenger plane
ut is the old name of the first note of the scale, now doh

explanation.surface: Someone gets off an aircraft and leaves a message so a bush can be delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' drops I, leaving ARBUS before the note goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is the arbutus, an evergreen shrub with red fruit.

clue.text: Wine prescribed by physician, more or less extreme

indicators.note: prescribed is read as pre-scribed, written after the physician

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
c. is circa, meaning approximately

explanation.surface: A doctor orders a bottle of wine as a fairly radical remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme ones, severe and far-reaching.

clue.text: Large variation produced enigma

definitions.note: the definition is a description, the one who produced Enigma

indicators.note: a variation reshuffles the letters of the word large

explanation.surface: A big variation created a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Enigma Variations is Elgar's orchestral work, so 'variation' does double duty in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer wrote the Enigma Variations, so he is the person who produced Enigma.

clue.text: Stone from eruption

explanation.surface: A gem comes out of a volcanic outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, a garnet, and also a boil or skin eruption.

clue.text: Best if you cut to me?

explanation.surface: Card players decide the best arrangement for the cut.
explanation.walkthrough: In cards, after one player cuts the pack, the other deals: 'if you cut, I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The best is the perfect one, and 'I deal' is what follows a cut to me.

clue.text: Bigmouth returned some very sad clothing

indicators.note: the whole run of letters is returned, read from right to left
only some of the word for very sad is used, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: tragic means very sad
garb means clothing

explanation.surface: A loudmouth sent back some very depressing outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims the end off the very-sad word to TRAG; 'returned' turns the whole run TRAGGARB round.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a boastful person, a loudmouth who brags.

clue.text: How workers in two shifts smile crookedly at one on river quiz

indicators.note: the workers are put in the shifted letters
the letters of how and two shift into new places

parts.note: ants are the standard crossword workers
beam means smile broadly
ill means badly or crookedly
I is the Roman numeral one
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Two shifts of workers grin wryly at someone by the river, wondering how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' rearranges the two words into WHO W TO; 'at' is a link. Contestants on the show use lifelines, which the other quiz clues define.
explanation.definitionFit: The television quiz show offers a seven-figure prize to its contestants.

clue.text: Fail due to wrong turn from Toulouse

indicators.note: wrong signals a faulty, rearranged order of letters
the turn is taken from the town's name

parts.note: U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: A driver misses out after a bad turn on leaving Toulouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes U out of TOULOUSE, leaving TOLOUSE, which 'wrong' rearranges. 'due to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose out is to fail to gain something, to miss an advantage.

clue.text: Passed, not by bypass

explanation.surface: Someone drove past, taking the town road rather than the ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: Being finished with an exam means one is passed, and the route through a town is the one avoiding the bypass.

clue.text: Imperial cat?

explanation.surface: Is this a regal kind of feline?
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is an imperial unit of weight, and also the snow leopard.

clue.text: Inaction is bad for a plant

indicators.note: the word inaction going bad means its letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing nothing harms a growing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is bad' rearranges INACTION; A is added. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotiana is the tobacco plant genus, grown for its scented flowers.

clue.text: Executed agitator keeping revolutionary Western idol

indicators.note: the agitator keeps the revolutionary inside him

parts.note: Nicola Sacco, the Italian-American anarchist executed in 1927 with Vanzetti
a red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A put-to-death firebrand holding a radical becomes a Western hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or person treated as beyond criticism, an idol.

clue.text: Eliot's village — his first — the third kept by a fireman

indicators.note: his first refers to Eliot's initial letter
the third letter is kept inside the fireman

parts.note: a stoker tends the fire of a furnace or locomotive
C is the third letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A poet's village is described through a fireman holding something third.
explanation.walkthrough: East Coker in Somerset is where T S Eliot's ancestors lived; it names one of his Four Quartets.
explanation.definitionFit: East Coker is a Somerset village, the setting and title of an Eliot poem.

clue.text: Inclination in a batsman from Trinidad to Spanish Town

indicators.note: the inclination goes in the run a plus batsman

parts.note: Brian Lara is the great Trinidadian batsman
cant means tilt or slope

explanation.surface: A Trinidadian cricketer leans while travelling to a town in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcantara is a town in western Spain, famous for its Roman bridge.

clue.text: Beethoven's seventh key, first from the greater

parts.note: Beethoven's Seventh Symphony is in A major
I is the Roman numeral for one, first

explanation.surface: A music lover names the key of Beethoven's Seventh, the first of the greater works.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Latin: 'a majori' means from the greater, as in arguing a majori ad minus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase translates literally as from the greater, used in logic.

clue.text: See 24
Brilliance of Martin on stage

explanation.surface: An actor named Martin dazzles on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a shine or lustre, and Martin Sheen is an American actor.

clue.text: The essence of good humour at a Fianna Fail rally

indicators.note: of signals letters taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Good cheer was the spirit of a political party's gathering in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Fianna Fail is an Irish political party; 'Fail rally' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond-flavoured essence used in baking, also a liqueur.

clue.text: L is half an option in 10 1

explanation.surface: The Roman letter L is half a lifeline on the quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral for fifty; fifty-fifty is a lifeline in 10 1, so half of it is one word.
explanation.definitionFit: L is the Roman numeral for the number, and the fifty-fifty lifeline halves into it.

clue.text: Precise form of culinary instructions

indicators.note: a new form of the word precise reshapes its letters

explanation.surface: Exact wording is how cooking directions are set out.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes are instructions for preparing dishes in the kitchen.

clue.text: Heap of dinner prepared as an option in 10 1

indicators.note: the words are prepared, made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A pile of supper is cooked up as one of the choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges HEAP OF DINNER. The definition is a lifeline on the quiz show at 10 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing an acquaintance for help is a lifeline on the quiz show.

clue.text: Adolescent predilection for veal?

explanation.surface: A teenager's crush turns out to be a taste for veal.
explanation.walkthrough: Veal is calf meat, so a fondness for eating it would be love of calf: the pun on the teenage crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf love is a youthful infatuation, puppy love.

clue.text: Fatal blow squashing trifle coming from the East, as Bush would have it

definitions.text: Fatal blow squashing trifle coming from the East, as Bush would have it

indicators.note: the blow squashes the trifle between its two letters

parts.note: KO is a knockout, a finishing blow

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value

explanation.surface: President Bush would have given the climate treaty a knockout blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from the East' turns the trifle into YOT. George W Bush rejected the Kyoto climate protocol, so the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyoto Protocol on emissions was rejected by Bush, who wished it knocked out.

clue.text: She was Fanny, with her last success in former scale only

indicators.note: the letter and the success go in the ladder

parts.note: scale formerly meant a ladder, from Latin scala

indicators.note: her last refers to the final letter of the name Fanny

parts.note: a win is a success
mere means only

explanation.surface: A woman once called Fanny owes her final triumph to a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Windermere's Fan is Oscar Wilde's play, so the heroine had a fan: 'Fanny'.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title heroine of Wilde's comedy, a woman named in the answer.
